records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:84 — If creation of a later worker fails, already-started workers are left running after SpanFlusher construction aborts.
records.rationale: Looking at the _create_processes method (lines 78-81), it loops through process_to_shards_map and calls _create_process_for_shards for each process_index. The _create_process_for_shards method (lines 83-117) creates and starts a process, storing it in self.processes[process_index]. If an exception occurs during creation of a later process (e.g., process_index 2), the already-started processes (process_index 0 and 1) remain running with no cleanup. records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:341 — Once the join deadline is exhausted, the loop skips terminating every remaining worker and can leave hung flushers running after shutdown returns.
records.rationale: Looking at the join() method in lines 326-347, when the deadline is exhausted (remaining_time <= 0), the code breaks out of the outer for loop at line 337. This means any remaining processes in self.processes that haven't been iterated yet will never have their terminate() called. The terminate() call at line 347 is inside the for loop, so breaking early skips termination for all remaining processes. This is a real bug where hung flusher processes could be left running after shutdown.
